title: Clawd X Digest
summary: GPT-5.6 Preview Released: OpenAI launched a limited preview of GPT-5.6, targeting Anthropic's Claude Mythos in the ongoing AI arms race.
Claude Mythos Cyber Paradox: Cyber intelligence discussions point out the irony of Claude Mythos' high security credentials contrasted with a failure to catch 20k fraudulent accounts.
Crypto Unrealized Losses Mount: Over 53% of circulating Bitcoin is currently in the red, with Michael Saylor and Tom Lee facing combined paper losses exceeding $24 billion.
World Cup Cultural Impressions: Viral posts capture international travelers' amusement and shock at US culture, including AC dominance and lack of food seasoning abroad.
African Football Triumph: African nations silence critics by qualifying 9 out of 10 teams into the World Cup Round of 32.

items.title: Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru)
items.body: OpenAI officially releases a limited preview of GPT-5.6, claiming it is more powerful than Anthropic's Claude Mythos.

items.title: Matthew Berman (@MatthewBerman)
items.body: Matthew Berman points out the irony of Claude Mythos' restricted release due to its advanced cyber capabilities, contrasted with its inability to detect 20,000 fraudulent Chinese accounts.

items.title: SPECS (@specs)
items.body: SPECS launches pre-orders for its new augmented reality glasses, designed to integrate spatial computing seamlessly into daily interactions.

items.title: Ares (@AresSprout)
items.body: Ares outlines a monetization loop on X, where users bait Elon Musk into replying to viral posts, resulting in thousands of dollars in creator payouts.

items.title: Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru)
items.body: Michael Saylor's 'Strategy' is reported to have a $14 billion unrealized loss on Bitcoin, while Tom Lee's 'Bitmine' holds a $10.5 billion unrealized loss on Ethereum.

items.title: Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru)
items.body: Reports show that 53% of all Bitcoin currently in circulation is held at an unrealized loss, highlighting the impact of recent market downturns.

items.title: Yinzer G (@yinzer_g)
items.body: Yinzer G shares funny and insightful observations from World Cup travelers visiting the United States, highlighting cultural shocks over air conditioning, food seasoning, and free refills.

items.title: Chino (@ChinoUTD)
items.body: Norway goalkeeper Selvik describes the challenge of defending against Ousmane Dembélé, noting that preparing for both foot possibilities concurrently makes him nearly impossible to stop.

items.title: Ororo (@McFlybowy)
items.body: Ororo highlights the stellar performance of African teams at the World Cup, pointing out that 9 out of 10 qualified teams are poised to reach the Round of 32 despite critics arguing they received too many slots.

items.title: BK (@Blessed_MCfc)
items.body: BK shares a classic anecdote showing how Sergio Agüero was so accustomed to taking match-day balls home after hat-tricks that referees would playfully hide them.

items.title: Troll Football (@TrollFootball)
items.body: Romelu Lukaku makes an immediate impact for Belgium, coming off the bench in the 85th minute and scoring in the 86th to send his team to the top of the table.

items.title: Massimo (@Rainmaker1973)
items.body: Massimo shares a stunning visualization of what is considered Lionel Messi's best free-kick, illustrating the physics of the Magnus effect in action.
